steps: Create a Slack app for your workspace (api.slack.com/apps, Create New App)
Under OAuth and Permissions add the bot scopes the agents need (for example channels:read and chat:write) and install the app to the workspace
Copy the Bot User OAuth Token (it starts with xoxb-)
Connect with it: switchboard connect slack --token-stdin  (paste the token, or pipe it in)

Browser OAuth instead needs an https redirect URL (see the note below): register a client with switchboard authconfig add slack ... --redirect-uri https://your-tunnel.example/oauth/callback, then switchboard connect slack --auth oauth2
notes: Slack states that the redirect_uri must use HTTPS and gives no loopback exception (docs: installing with OAuth), so the OAuth flow is refused for a plain http loopback callback. The bot token above avoids the problem.
Slack sends the app credentials as form fields and the docs do not mention PKCE; scopes are comma separated.
Token rotation (refresh tokens that expire) exists for apps with granular permissions and is optional; the engine refreshes when a refresh token is present.
Slack reports a failed token exchange as HTTP 200 with ok:false; the engine reads the body.
